en.title: Java try / catch / finally — Console Trace
en.description:
You are given the integer inputs to the original divide(a,b) code. When the division throws, catch prints `Exception `; finally always prints `Finally `. The return value is never printed. Added by this site: to make standard output judgeable, the text produced on System.err in chronological order is merged into a single console trace.

The input protocol and the generalized ranges are additions by this site; they do not mean the original problem used stdin/stdout.
en.input: One line with two signed 32-bit integers a, b.
en.output: Output the console text in the original code's execution order: `Exception Finally` when b=0, otherwise `Finally`.
en.explanation: See the accompanying editorial for the approach, correctness, and complexity.
hints: Trace the state changes step by step; pay special attention to when the increment in the loop condition happens and to the execution order of finally.
